context: Owner decisions 2026-11-27 (dialog): (1) TPC-DS sub-scale: carry the 72-line tpcgen-rs #677 patch (pin tpcdsgen to a BenchBox-dev/tpcgen-rs commit = v4.0.0 + #677), delete own dsgen/ generators, return to crates.io when released. (2) Upstream-gap rule: no divergent fork; a carried patch only if <= ~200 changed lines, submitted upstream, pinned by commit, listed in README with its upstream PR; anything larger goes to the owner with sizes first. (3) TPC-DS refresh sets: keep own code in its own PR, finish SF 100 parity, offer upstream; required before C removal, not before the TPC cutover. (4) Acceptance: a metric passes inside legacy min-max or the 99.9% prediction interval from 5 legacy seeds; boundary quantiles on low-cardinality columns by rank. (5) Empty queries: must return rows on every seed where legacy does on every seed; where legacy is sometimes empty, the library may be empty on no more seeds than legacy. (6) SSB row counts follow the SSB specification (part = 200,000 x floor(1 + log2 SF), date = 2,556). (7) Oracle defects: qgen seed 0 for Q7/Q12 raises a clear error; the 13 nondeterministic dsqgen cases are excluded only with recorded proof and the library is deterministic for them. (8) Licensing: proceed; ship the TPC legal notice in wheels, templates and tpcds.idx stay in BenchBox, record the position in the licensing doc. (9) Until the review gate posts its first verdict, library PRs may merge with green CI plus an independent reviewer agent reporting no Critical/High/Medium findings; afterwards the gate is required. (10) BenchBox native-datagen extra may be developed and CI-tested against wheels built from a pinned library commit; the BenchBox PR adding the extra merges only after the PyPI release exists. (11) Lock-waiter kills: investigate and report only; no kill-policy change. Scope is investigation and a report with a proposed fix; acceptance items 2 and 3 (policy and code change) need a later owner approval.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-26 `make pr-preflight` in BenchBox.wt-parquet-v2 was terminated by SIGTERM (rc 143, `make: *** [pr-preflight] Terminated: 15`) three times while waiting on the host test lock; once after its pytest step had passed (5,730 passed), leaving no receipt. The sentinel log at 15:06 shows pressure level 2 with the waiting `host_lock run --phase linux-preflight` process (0.06 GiB) listed among candidates. A waiter that uses almost no memory should not be killed, and a killed preflight should leave a clear failure record.

## Change
Find the sender and write a report proposing a fix with its risk; no code or policy change (owner decision 11).

## Decision gates
- If the sentinel is not the sender, record the real sender before changing anything.
- Do not weaken the memory budget or disable the watchdog; owner approval is needed for any change to kill policy.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, make agent-write-preflight); the primary clone is read-only.
- Heavy work only through make heavy-run; never bypass or signal the lock, and never kill processes by name pattern (pkill -f); stop only PIDs you started.
- Commits as the configured human identity; no agent attribution.
- A choice between a small and a large implementation path goes to the owner with sizes before work starts.
- Report only results that were observed; name anything not run.
